newsitem.title: UK: BAA buying Duty Free International for $674 million.
newsitem.headline: BAA buying Duty Free International for $674 million.

text.p: Britain's BAA Plc, which operates seven British airports including Heathrow and Gatwick near London, said Thursday it agreed to buy U.S. duty-free retailer Duty Free International Inc. for about $674 million.

In its first major acquisition in eight years, BAA agreed to pay $24 a share for New York-based DFI, the fifth-largest duty- and tax-free business in the world. DFI stock rose $3.625 to $23.75 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.

The company said the deal would make BAA the second-largest duty- and tax-free business in the world after Duty Free Shoppers, which is owned by LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton, the French maker of champagne, handbags and other luxury goods.
DFI, based in New York, sells tobacco, liquor, perfumes, cosmetics, jewelry and other gift items, free of excise taxes and duties, at about 175 stores at airports and other locations.
In its latest fiscal year ended in January, it earned about $21.4 million, or 79 cents a share, on sales of $571 million.

"We are trying to grow and become a global player in the world duty-free market and we would like to continue growing both organically and perhaps by further joint ventures or acquisitions," BAA Finance Director Russell Walls said in an interview.
But he said the company has no specific plans for more acquisition at present.

"By acquiring another large business unaffected by the possible loss of European duty free, we will be able to protect and enhance profits, bring improved merchandising to DFI ... and further develop the business," BAA Chief Executive John Egan said.

In addition to airport shops, DFI operates in-flight duty free shopping services, Canadian and Mexican border duty-free stores and a diplomatic and wholesale operation serving embassies and cruise ship ports.
BAA plans to fund the acquisition from existing resources and does not expect the purchase to hurt its earnings.
On the contrary, finance director Walls said that the purchase would probably enhance BAA earnings "reasonably quickly."
